entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded, socially conferred normative relation that inheres in an agent (the bearer) and attaches a specific obligation to that agent. This is paradigmatically a Role in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant, inheres in exactly one agent bearer, and is externally grounded in the institutional/legal context that generates the obligation. It is distinct from the obligation itself (LegalObligation, already typed as BFO_0000023) in that it captures the relational binding-to-agent aspect. However, it is closely related; see open questions.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because it is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent and is conferred by the social/legal context.

AgentObligationBinding specializes LegalObligation by adding the aspect of direct binding to a specific agent bearer; this makes it a subclass of the already-defined LegalObligation role class. This is a candidate relation pending user confirmation.

open_questions: Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of LegalObligation (the already-existing role class), or should it be a sibling class under BFO_0000023 that stands in a distinct relation to LegalObligation?

Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended to denote the relational tie (a role inhering in the agent) or the obligation content itself (a generically dependent continuant, i.e., the norm)? If the latter, BFO_0000031 (GDC) would be more appropriate.
Is 'agent' here restricted to legal persons, or does it also include organizations, AI systems, or other non-human bearers? This affects what the domain of the 'inheres in' relation should be.

Should this concept be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Role, if the emphasis is on an internally grounded capacity of the agent to be bound rather than an externally conferred status?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' most naturally denotes the normative tie that attaches an obligation to a specific agent — i.e., the fact that an agent bears a particular obligation. In BFO terms, this is a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020) that inheres in the agent as its bearer. Because the binding is externally grounded in social/legal context (not in the agent's intrinsic nature), it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition. It is proposed as a new class AgentObligationBinding, subclassing the existing LegalObligation class (itself already typed under BFO_0000023), since it represents the particularized, agent-directed instantiation of a legal obligation. Key open questions remain about whether the intended meaning is the relational binding (role), the norm content (GDC), or a capacity (disposition), and whether the subclass relationship to LegalObligation is appropriate.
